lessons.title: What permaculture is
lessons.html:
Farming like nature

Permaculture is a way of growing food that copies nature. In a natural forest or veld, nobody adds fertiliser or sprays, but plants still grow well. This is because many kinds of plants and animals live together, leaves fall and feed the soil, and water soaks in. Permaculture tries to build gardens and farms that work in the same way.

Many home gardens, school gardens and community gardens in South Africa use permaculture to grow food with little money.

The three ethics: caring

  • Care for the earth – look after the soil, water, plants and animals.
  • Care for people – grow healthy food for families and the community.
  • Share fairly – take what you need and share the extra with others, or put it back into the garden.

Some simple principles

PrincipleWhat it means
Watch firstBefore you plant, watch where the sun shines, where water runs and where the wind blows
Catch and keep waterCollect rain from roofs in tanks; make the soil hold water with mulch
Waste nothingTurn kitchen scraps, leaves and manure into compost
Many kinds of plantsGrow many different crops together; if one fails, others still give food
Everything helps something elseChickens give eggs, manure and eat insects; trees give fruit, shade and leaves for mulch
Start smallStart with one bed and look after it well, then grow bigger

Example

Mama Nomsa has a small yard. She puts a rain tank on her roof, makes compost from kitchen scraps, and grows spinach, onions, beans, pumpkins and a peach tree close together. Her chickens eat insects and give manure for the compost. She spends very little money and has food all year.

lessons.title: Putting the principles into practice
lessons.html:
Look after the soil

Healthy soil is the start of a good garden.

  • Compost – make a heap of green material (fresh leaves, vegetable scraps, fresh manure) and brown material (dry leaves, dry grass, straw). Keep it damp and turn it now and then. In a few months it becomes dark, crumbly compost.
  • Mulch – cover the soil around plants with dry grass, leaves or straw. Mulch keeps the soil cool and wet, stops weeds and slowly feeds the soil.
  • Do not leave soil bare. Bare soil dries out and blows or washes away.
  • Do not burn leaves and grass. Use them for compost and mulch.

Save water

  • Collect rainwater from roofs in tanks or drums.
  • Water early in the morning or late in the afternoon, at the roots, not on the leaves.
  • Use mulch so less water is lost.
  • Make small trenches across the slope so rainwater soaks in and does not run away.

Plant in a smart way

  • Plant things you use every day, like herbs and spinach, close to the kitchen door.
  • Put plants that need less care, like fruit trees, further away.
  • Mix plants: for example plant maize, beans and pumpkins together. Beans feed the soil, maize gives the beans something to climb, pumpkin leaves cover the soil.
  • Plant flowers like marigolds and herbs among vegetables. They bring helpful insects.
  • Save your own seed from the best plants.

Control pests naturally

  • Many different plants mean pests do not spread as easily.
  • Birds, frogs, ladybirds and spiders eat pests. Do not kill them.
  • Pick off caterpillars and snails by hand.

Key points

  • Permaculture copies nature to grow food with little cost.
  • Its ethics are care for the earth, care for people and share fairly.
  • Make compost and use mulch; never leave soil bare.
  • Catch rainwater and water at the roots.
  • Mix many plants together and let natural helpers control pests.

quiz.question: What does permaculture try to copy?

options.text: Nature, such as a forest or the veld

quiz.question: Which is one of the three permaculture ethics?

options.text: Makes the soil hot and dry
Keeps the soil cool and wet and stops weeds

quiz.question: Where should you plant herbs and spinach that you use every day?

options.text: Far away at the end of the plot

quiz.question: Why grow many kinds of plants together?

options.text: If one fails, others still give food, and pests spread less

quiz.question: In permaculture, leaves and dry grass should be burned.
Ladybirds, frogs and birds help control pests in the garden.
Which are good ways to save water in a permaculture garden? (select all that apply)

Water the leaves in the hot midday sun
